items.title: Grocery Prices Sit 22% Above 2021 Levels as Near-Record Diesel Raises Costs From Farm to Store
items.excerpt: September price data show food at home costs 22.5% more than five years ago, while diesel above $6 a gallon adds pressure that has not fully reached store shelves. ... Americans are paying about 22% more for groceries than they did five years ago, and the latest federal price data arrived as diesel — the fuel that powers tractors, freight trucks and refrigerated trailers — holds near its record high. The Bureau of Labor Statistics' food-at-home index stood at 321.758 in September 2026, compared with 262.695 in September 2021, a 22.5% increase, according to BLS figures compiled by the St. Louis Fed. The monthly picture looks calmer. Grocery prices slipped 0.1% in September and were 1.8% higher than a year earlier, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported in its latest Consumer Price Index release. But a slower annual rate does not erase five years of accumulated increases, and several of the foods most closely tied to a balanced diet are still rising faster than the grocery average. ... Fuel is what makes the next few months hard to call. The national average price of diesel was $6.33 a gallon on Oct. 16, up 68% from $3.76 before the U.S.-Iran war began, according to AAA figures cited by the Associated Press. Diesel hit a record $6.53 in September. No federal agency has yet measured how much of that cost will reach retail food prices, and economists quoted by the AP said much of it has not shown up so far. ... The September report shows a split grocery aisle. Fresh fruits were up 4.9% from a year earlier, fruits and vegetables overall rose 3.7%, coffee climbed 7.1%, and beef rose 3.5%, according to the BLS detailed tables. Eggs fell 20.6%, and dairy dipped 0.7%, which helped hold the overall grocery figure down. ... Eating out remains the bigger budget strain. Prices for food away from home rose 3.5% over the year, nearly double the grocery rate. The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Economic Research Service now forecasts grocery prices will rise 2.4% in 2026, with fresh vegetables up 5.7% and beef and veal up 9.4%, while eggs are expected to fall 29.4%. The AP reported that USDA's forecast before the war called for a 1.7% grocery increase this year. ... The fuel effect starts on the farm. A Farm Bureau analysis by Deputy Chief Economist Faith Parum and Associate Economist Cameron Castillo found farm diesel in Illinois, as reported by USDA's ... Freight data point the same way. September producer-price data showed truck freight prices up 19.3% from a year earlier, while transportation and warehousing of goods sold to businesses cost 10.2% more, the AP reported. Those indexes track what carriers charge, not what shoppers pay. USDA also raised its 2026 estimates of fuel, lubricant and electricity costs for major crops by 33% to 41%, according to the AP.

items.title: Inflation Overshot Expectations in September | Fifth Third Bank
items.excerpt: Inflation surprised to the upside in September. Headline CPI matched expectations for the month, accelerating to 0.6% from 0.4% on a 9.1% jump in gasoline prices. The negative surprise was in core prices, which rose a faster-than-expected 0.3%. Price increases were widespread across the core CPI basket, affecting a range of durable goods, nondurables, and services. The PPI rose even more than the CPI, up 1.3% versus the 0.6% expected. Diesel surged a seasonally adjusted 21.0%. Producer prices for foods rose 1.2% on double-digit increases of fresh and dry vegetables, hay and hayseeds, grains, and oilseeds—rising prices of livestock feeds will likely translate to more expensive meat in 2027. Core PPI excluding food and energy rose 0.7% as trade services (Wholesale and retail margins) climbed 1.4% and energy-intensive transportation and warehousing charges jumped 3.4%. A silver lining is that many of the core PPI components that carry over into PCE inflation behaved better than the headline.

items.title: US inflation rose slightly last month after 2 years of steady cooling but remained low
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON (AP) — Inflation in the United States ticked up in October, driven by costlier rents, used cars and air fares, a sign that price increases might be leveling off after having slowed in September to their lowest pace since 2021. Consumer prices rose 2.6% from a year earlier, the Labor Department said Wednesday, up from 2.4% in September. It was the first rise in annual inflation in seven months. From September to October, prices edged up 0.2%, the same as the previous month. Excluding volatile food and energy costs, “core” prices rose 3.3% from a year earlier, the same as in September. From September to October, core prices rose 0.3% for a third straight month. Over the long run, core inflation at that pace would exceed the Fed’s 2% target. An uptick in prices, if sustained, could stir concerns in financial markets that progress in taming inflation may be slowing. It might also make the Federal Reserve less inclined to cut its key interest rate in the coming months, as its officials have previously indicated they likely would. ... Still, most economists think inflation will eventually resume its slowdown. Consumer inflation, which peaked at 9.1% in 2022, has since fallen steadily, though overall prices are still about 20% higher than they were three years ago. ... In addition, the economy is growing faster than many economists had expected earlier this year. It has expanded at nearly a 3% annual rate over the past six months, with consumers, particularly those with higher incomes, spending freely and fueling growth. ... At a news conference last week, Fed Chair Jerome Powell expressed confidence that inflation is still heading down to the central bank’s 2% target, though perhaps slowly and unevenly. Powell also noted that most sources of price pressures are cooling, suggesting that inflation isn’t likely to accelerate in the coming months. Wages are still growing and have outpaced prices for the past year and a half. But Powell noted that wages aren’t rising quickly enough to boost inflation. ... A survey released Tuesday by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York found that consumers expect prices to rise just 2.9% in the next 12 months, which would be the lowest such measure in nearly four years. Lower inflation expectations are important because when consumers expect milder price increases, they’re less likely to act in ways that raise inflation, such as accelerating their purchases or demanding higher pay to offset higher prices.

items.excerpt: Ozzy Osbourne Was ‘Flying High’ Until the ‘Day He Passed’ After Final Concert, Sharon Osbourne Says: ‘We Hadn’t Seen Him That Way in Years’ and more — today's film signal. The world of film is abuzz with a mix of nostalgia, celebration, and innovation, as today's headlines weave a narrative that takes us on a journey from the past to the present. We start with a poignant reflection on the life of a rock legend, Ozzy Osbourne, whose final concert marked a high point before his passing, according to his wife Sharon Osbourne. This somber note is balanced by the excitement of upcoming film competitions, such as the Tokyo Filmex, which will feature Oscar entries from Thailand and Nepal, and boast a jury that includes the acclaimed Lee Kang-sheng. As we delve deeper into the day's news, we find ourselves reminiscing about classic films, thanks to Julia Stiles' emotional reunion with her '10 Things I Hate About You' castmates on 'Dancing With the Stars', which included a heartfelt tribute to the late Heath Ledger. The film world is also looking to the future, with the announcement of Disney+'s and Hulu's Japanese horror series 'Night Tales Club', which boasts an impressive lineup of directors, including Kurosawa Kiyoshi and Shimizu Takashi. Meanwhile, the Access: Horror Virtual Film Festival is pushing boundaries by challenging traditional horror tropes and shedding light on disability in a unique and thought-provoking way, making for a truly diverse and captivating day in the world of film. Entertainment News (10/21/26) - BusinessWorld Online # Entertainment News (10/21/26) PRODUCER, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Ziv has teamed up with rising P-pop girl group VVINK for “Trisikulo,” a pop track on the familiar third-wheel experience. October 20, 2026 | 6:06 pm ## Ziv, VVINK release collaboration PRODUCER, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Ziv has teamed up with rising P-pop girl group VVINK for “Trisikulo,” a pop track on the familiar third-wheel experience. Released under Sony Music Entertainment, it is built around Filipino wordplay that links a tricycle’s three wheels to the feeling of being the extra person in someone else’s love story. The song was co-written by Ziv alongside Paolo Benjamin Guico of Filipino folk-pop band Ben&Ben and Angelika Samantha Ortiz, one of the songwriters behind BINI’s hit “Pantropiko.” The mixing was also done by Jacques Jenkins and mastering by Luna Tebbs. The track is out now on all digital music streaming platforms. ## *Love in Disguise* premieres on Prime Video *LOVE in Disguise*, a Korean series based on the hit web novel *Why Don’t You Know It’s a Girl?*, has premiered on Prime Video. It is directed by Park Dhan-hee and stars Yim Si Wan, Seorina, Kim Junghyun, and Yeonwoo. The genre-blending romance is exclusively seen on Prime Video in the Philippines and in more than 240 countries and territories worldwide. ## Estelle Fly drops club-pop single SINGAPOREAN pop artist Estelle Fly has released “Shut It Down,” a playful club-pop single about switching off the overthinking and making the dance floor your own. Inspired by the Rihanna and Kesha songs, the new release is an invitation to let loose, dance with friends and have fun even when life feels complicated. It is out now on all digital music streaming

items.excerpt: Starting with the latest developments in the Tiger Shroff firing case, the investigation has led to more arrests. After three suspected shooters were apprehended in Kota, the Delhi Police Special Cell arrested four additional accused on Tuesday. According to The Hindu, they are suspected of transporting a firearm to Mumbai and helping coordinate the operation allegedly connected to the attack on Tiger Shroff. With just days left before its grand theatrical release, Ramayana: Part 1, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, has made headlines after being declared tax-free in West Bengal by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Check out all the live updates below: ... ## Tiger Shroff Firing Probe: Five More Persons Held Five more persons, including two women, have been nabbed from Haryana and Uttar Pradesh as the investigation into actor Tiger Shroff firing case is being expanded to unravel a firearm-supplying network and other aspects, a Mumbai Police officer said on Wednesday. Addressing a press conference, DCP Raj Tilak Roshan said the five individuals are being brought to Mumbai, taking the total number of arrests in the case to eight so far. Earlier in the day, three key accused allegedly involved in firing at Shroff's car on Sunday were brought to Mumbai from Kota in Rajasthan and sent to police custody till October 31. ... ## Tiger Shroff Back On Lag Jaa Gale Sets After Firing Incident Days after unidentified assailiants attacked Tiger Shroff, the actor has reportedly returned to the sets of his upcoming film Lag Jaa Gale which also features Janhvi Kapoor and Lakshya in the lead. ... ## Jailer 2 Box Office Collection Day 6: Rajinikanth's Film Crosses ₹540 Cr Worldwide Rajinikanth's Tamil action comedy Jailer 2 continued its theatrical run with an increase in domestic net collections on Tuesday, October 20. According to Sacnilk's estimates, the film earned ₹45.55 crore net in India on Day 6, taking its cumulative India net collection to ₹287.80 crore. With its overseas earnings also contributing to the total, the film's worldwide gross collection reached ₹541 crore. Following Tuesday's earnings, Jailer 2's India net collection stood at ₹287.80 crore, while its domestic gross collection reached ₹337 crore. Overseas markets contributed an estimated ₹10 crore gross on Day 6, taking the film's cumulative overseas gross to ₹204 crore. Combining the domestic and overseas figures, the film's worldwide gross collection reached ₹541 crore after six days. ... ## Ranbir Kapoor’s ‘Ramayana’ Declared Tax-Free In Bengal Ahead Of Grand Theatrical Release On November 5 Nitesh Tiwari’s upcoming cinematic adaptation of the Hindu epic Ramayana, featuring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Yash as Ravana, has been declared tax-free in West Bengal. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced the decision on Dussehra, ahead of the film’s scheduled theatrical release on November 5, 2026. Speaking to ANI, Adhikari confirmed the move and referred to other films that have received similar treatment. He said, "The Ramayana film has been made tax-free. The Kerala Story, The Kashmir Files, and The Bengal Files—all of these will be (or have been) made tax-free, and the same will apply to Ramayana. In the days to come, we will see films on Shri Krishna and Arjuna, as well as the Mahabharata..." ... The Delhi Police Special Cell’s Northern Range (NDR) unit arrested four people on Tuesday in connection with an alleged arms supply network linked to the October 18 firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai, a senior police official confirmed. The accused have been identified as Kunal, 21, and Sumit, 19, both from Haryana’s Sonipat district, along with Radha, 23, and Babita, 23, who are residents of Uttar Pradesh.
